This person is a 42-year-old owner of a 20-employee precision engineering SME in Coventry exporting most components to Germany and France; they want the UK to prioritize re-entry to the customs union and single market for goods, remove rules of origin, re-align product standards to CE marking to avoid duplicate UKCA testing, and integrate fully with EU transit and customs IT so just-in-time deliveries stop missing slots; they care because border friction since 2021 forced them to hold costly buffer stock and they lost an Italian client over certification delays.

This person is a 55-year-old CEO of a Leeds-based medical device manufacturer that invested heavily in UKCA-only labeling and MHRA approvals; they oppose a rapid rejoin unless there is a multi-year grandfathering period for UKCA certificates, reciprocal acceptance of MHRA-assessed clinical evidence under EU MDR, and grant support for relabeling lines; they care because they spent £1.2m retooling for UKCA and a sudden switch back to CE would strand inventory and invalidate packaging artwork already printed.

This person is the HR director of an NHS trust in Cornwall facing double-digit nurse vacancy rates; they want early restoration of freedom of movement for health occupations, automatic mutual recognition of nursing and midwifery qualifications, a temporary bridging visa for EEA clinicians during the accession period, and removal of the immigration health surcharge for NHS recruits; they care because agency spend is unsustainable and current salary thresholds and visa fees are blocking hires.

This person is a Border Force union representative at Dover; they want any rejoin policy to retain UK non-participation in Schengen and full control over visa policy, with negotiated protocols that preserve UK primary border checks and clear investment in exit/entry systems integration without accepting Schengen acquis obligations; they care because staffing, rostering, and infrastructure are built around current controls and abrupt changes could compromise security and working conditions.

This person is a 34-year-old UK citizen in Birmingham married to a Polish architect on pre-settled status; they want early adoption of EU free movement provisions, no-fee conversion of settled and pre-settled statuses to EU residence rights, and restoration of mutual recognition of professional qualifications so the spouse can work on EU projects without duplicative licensing; they care because visa renewal anxiety and lost work opportunities in Germany have delayed buying a home and starting their own firm.

This person is a 68-year-old sovereignty campaigner in Hartlepool who canvassed for Brexit; they will only accept any rejoin process that includes a national referendum, explicit parliamentary safeguards against automatic supremacy of EU law, and firm political assurances that the UK will not be obliged to adopt the euro or join Schengen; they care because they believe border control, lawmaking, and trade policy should remain fully accountable to Westminster voters.

This person is a 49-year-old trawler skipper from Peterhead landing cod and haddock; they oppose rejoining unless the UK secures improved quota shares under the Common Fisheries Policy, tight joint enforcement against foreign incursions in UK waters, and a multi-year compensation and fleet modernisation fund to manage any quota cuts; they care because their margins depend on allocations and they fear a return to what they view as unfair relative stability keys.

This person is a marine conservation scientist at an NGO in Brighton; they support rejoining to align with CFP ecosystem-based management, binding maximum sustainable yield targets, and joint control regimes, and want the UK to champion closed spawning areas, stronger bycatch rules, and transparent data sharing in EU councils; they care because fragmented post-Brexit governance has complicated stock assessments and undermined North Sea recovery plans.

This person is a 37-year-old arable farmer in Cambridgeshire whose basic payments declined under new domestic schemes; they want rejoining to reintroduce predictable CAP direct payments with eco-schemes compatible with their crop rotations, phased SPS alignment to smooth grain exports to EU buyers, and credit for recent environmental investments during the transition; they care because bank financing hinges on stable income streams and reliable market access.

This person is a low-income consumer advocate in Tower Hamlets working with food banks; they worry that rejoining without safeguards could raise food prices via CAP protections and constrain UK flexibility on VAT relief, so they want the UK to push for CAP reform toward targeted environmental payments, secure the ability to keep zero VAT on essentials within EU VAT rules, and fund targeted rebates for vulnerable households; they care because small price increases cascade into hunger for the people they support.

This person is a 42-year-old Midlands precision-engineering SME owner employing 75 people who exports 65% of turnover to Germany and the Netherlands; they want re-accession implemented with immediate re-entry to the Single Market and Customs Union, reinstatement of CE-marking acceptance and mutual recognition of conformity assessment, HMRC-funded vouchers for re-testing to EU standards, simplified CDS/GVMS processes and AEO fast-track for SMEs, and a 12-18 month transition where UKCA and CE markings are both valid to prevent scrapping inventory.

This person is a 58-year-old inshore fishing skipper from Newlyn, Cornwall whose income improved with post-Brexit quota gains; they will oppose rejoining unless the negotiating mandate secures multi-year derogations under the Common Fisheries Policy for small-scale fleets, legally binding minimum national quota shares above 2015 baselines, ring-fenced EMFAF-style support for gear changes and port infrastructure, and community co-management councils written into the accession treaty before Parliament ratifies.

This person is a 46-year-old NHS hospital HR director in Greater Manchester responsible for staffing 900 nurses; they want the implementation plan to front-load mutual recognition of professional qualifications under Directive 2005/36/EC, a joint NMC/GMC-EU fast-track desk to clear backlogs within 90 days, temporary bridging visas during the transition, immediate association to Erasmus+ to rebuild training pipelines, and portable pension and indemnity arrangements so EU clinicians can start safely on day one.

This person is a 29-year-old warehouse operative in Ashford, Kent on a zero-hours contract worried about wage undercutting and housing pressure; they insist the accession treaty include a time-limited safeguard clause that can temporarily restrict free movement if local unemployment or vacancy rates trigger thresholds, guaranteed funding to restore a Migration Impact Fund for councils, beefed-up HMRC enforcement against minimum wage abuses, and ring-fenced apprenticeships so any labour inflow is matched by skills investment.

This person is a 50-year-old operations manager at an agri-food processor in County Armagh, Northern Ireland juggling dual-regime paperwork; they want rejoining sequenced to remove Irish Sea checks by moving to a single UK-EU SPS and customs regime, a published timeline for when Windsor Framework easements sunset, expanded trusted-trader and green-lane schemes during the transition, and a one-stop helpline that clarifies when EU customs code will apply uniformly across GB and NI.

This person is a 39-year-old CFO of a Speyside whisky distillery exporting heavily to the US and Asia; they back rejoining only if the government simultaneously preserves continuity of post-Brexit FTAs by negotiating rollover clauses and cumulation fixes for rules of origin, secures tariff-rate quota access at least equal to current schedules, protects Scotch whisky geographical indications in both EU and non-EU markets, and publishes a legal instrument that prevents a cliff-edge loss of CPTPP and UK-Japan preferences during the EU accession transition.

This person is a 37-year-old Home Office caseworker in Sheffield who processes EU Settlement Scheme applications; they want a staged plan that preserves Withdrawal Agreement rights while reintroducing free movement, including legislation to merge or sunset EUSS without creating gaps in right-to-work and right-to-rent checks, investment to upgrade the Atlas caseworking IT and expand UKVCAS appointments, automatic conversion of pre-settled to settled status where eligible, a single digital status portal interoperable with DWP and HMRC, and clear guidance on ECJ jurisdiction over citizens' rights to avoid judicial review risk.

This person is a 62-year-old retired Army veteran in Lincolnshire who campaigned for sovereignty; if rejoining proceeds, they demand a legally binding referendum on the final accession treaty, retention of non-Schengen status and a formal euro opt-out protocol, selective opt-outs from Justice and Home Affairs akin to Denmark's, a parliamentary scrutiny reserve that requires Commons approval before ministers agree to new EU measures, and domestic legislation clarifying the limits of ECJ jurisdiction over UK criminal law.

This person is a 27-year-old tenant sheep and arable farmer in North Yorkshire on a tight margin; they want entry to the Common Agricultural Policy designed to avoid cash-flow gaps by phasing Basic Income Support while integrating England's ELM eco-schemes, a small-farm redistributive top-up, continuity in cross-compliance/conditionality so inspections are predictable, DEFRA-funded advisory support to navigate CAP IT systems, and interoperability of livestock movement data with TRACES so animals can move seamlessly to EU markets.

This person is a 48-year-old chartered accountant in Surrey active in a taxpayer advocacy group; they want the government to publish an itemised, OBR-scored forecast of gross and net EU budget contributions over 10 years, a negotiating objective for a rebate or contribution cap, a transparent dashboard comparing UK CAP receipts and structural funds to contributions by region, and a fiscal rule that any additional EU payments are offset by identified savings or tax measures, with NAO auditing of all transition costs.

This person is a 57-year-old care home owner in Cornwall who has struggled to fill vacancies since 2021 and wants any application to rejoin the EU to front-load labour mobility: they argue the government should file under Article 49 while simultaneously negotiating an interim mobility chapter targeted at health and social care, fast-track mutual recognition of nursing and care qualifications, and re-align with EU rules on professional credentials so their EU staff can be onboarded without months-long visa and verification delays.

This person is a 45-year-old Home Office border security policy lead in London who would only support rejoining if implementation is phased to protect border integrity: they want a clear timetable for reintroducing free movement with defined safeguard clauses, guaranteed preservation of the Common Travel Area with Ireland, funding to make UK systems interoperable with the EU Entry/Exit System and ETIAS, and a treaty protocol limiting the scope and timing of ECJ jurisdiction in policing and security cooperation during transition.

This person is a 38-year-old owner of a metal fabrication SME in the West Midlands who exports to France and Germany and wants the rejoin bid to prioritise frictionless trade: they call for rapid pre-alignment with the Union Customs Code, immediate return to CE marking instead of UKCA, joining the EU VAT One Stop Shop, and an accession roadmap that restores customs union membership and rules-of-origin relief on day one to end costly origin proofs and duplicate product conformity tests.

This person is a 52-year-old HMRC customs IT programme manager in Essex who worries about operational risk and insists the government pair any rejoin application with a two-year dual-running plan for border systems: they want funded integration of EU tariff and classification databases (TARIC) into the UK’s CDS, a legal timetable for import VAT changes, joint UK–EU testing of ICS2/NCTS interfaces, and clear statutory guidance to avoid a cliff-edge for businesses and ports.

This person is a 49-year-old inshore fishing skipper from Peterhead who fears losing access if the UK re-enters the Common Fisheries Policy and therefore wants the application conditioned on a bespoke fisheries protocol: they argue for protected 12-mile limits, a renegotiated quota share based on zonal attachment, seasonal closures set by UK scientific advice, and an EU-backed compensation fund to offset any effort reductions required by a return to the CFP.

This person is a 33-year-old seafood processor in Aberdeenshire whose export consignments have been delayed by post-Brexit health checks and wants rejoining sequenced to restore SPS alignment first: they propose that the UK’s application include an immediate veterinary agreement and electronic certification pilot, a guarantee of zero-tariff, zero-SPS frictions at accession, and a transition plan that keeps EU workers in processing plants through streamlined residence documentation.

This person is a 41-year-old university research grants director in Manchester who wants the application to rejoin to prioritise science and education: they advocate a negotiating sequence that immediately re-associates the UK to Horizon Europe and Erasmus+ during the accession process, restores ERC eligibility, secures GDPR adequacy to enable cross-border data sharing for research, and creates a joint committee to fast-track recognition of degrees and researcher mobility.

This person is a 68-year-old retired accountant in Doncaster on a fixed income who is open to rejoining only with strict fiscal safeguards: they demand an independent OBR-style assessment of net budget contributions, a negotiated correction mechanism akin to a rebate for the first Multiannual Financial Framework after accession, a public line-by-line account of CAP receipts versus contributions, and a binding referendum at treaty ratification so taxpayers can approve the final terms.

This person is a 44-year-old logistics operations manager in Belfast who manages GB–NI routes and wants rejoining to eliminate internal frictions: they argue the application must be sequenced so the entire UK re-enters the EU customs union and SPS regime simultaneously, rendering the Windsor Framework checks unnecessary, and they want guaranteed alignment of port systems and ferry schedules to avoid a new cliff-edge when the Irish Sea controls are switched off.

This person is a 36-year-old constitutional lawyer in Cambridge who prioritises domestic safeguards in any rejoin process: they want a detailed accession white paper, primary legislation to re-incorporate the acquis with clear parliamentary scrutiny and sunset clauses for delegated powers, explicit protocols on preliminary references to the ECJ, preservation of the Common Travel Area, and transparency over which former opt-outs (euro, Schengen, Justice and Home Affairs) the UK will seek and on what legal basis.
